summary: Iteration 5 full regression + new-feature testing (demo removal, admin-created driver accounts, weekly rotation engine, rest constraint, driver notifications, shift-swap workflow). Backend: 27/27 pytest PASS (backend_test.py rewritten for iter-5 semantics — old demo-dataset assertions removed). Frontend: verified /login has no demo buttons, admin creates driver with password (account-badge visible), new driver logs in and lands on read-only /tabellone with notif-bell, notif-count, my-rotation shown ('Mattino Presto') and 'Le mie richieste di cambio' section, admin /scambi page loads with approve/reject controls. No blocking issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: Login.jsx keeps a dead `quick`/`void quick;` stub after removing demo buttons — harmless but noise; can be deleted.

DriverView notif-bell and my-rotation render only after AuthContext resolves user (myId). This is correct, but automated tests must wait for the bell before asserting. Consider a small skeleton to signal loading state.

server.py remove_demo_data() also does `await db.shifts.delete_many({})` and `db.absences.delete_many({})` unconditionally on the one-time run — fine now, but a note in code that this runs only when app_meta.demo.removed is falsy would help future maintainers.

generate_shifts assigns weekday slots strictly by the weekly rotation map. If a driver's rotation slot has no matching qualified route for them in that week, they end up in `unassigned_drivers`. This is expected but should be surfaced clearly in the UI (already covered by Dashboard toast per PRD).
